Number of CPU Cores

Source: R/cpus.r
n_cpus.Rd

How many threads ecodive's functions use by default: the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it.

Usage

n_cpus()

Value

A scalar integer, at least 1. Always 1 where ecodive was built without pthread support.

Details

n_cpus() is the default for every function's cpus argument. It follows the checks of parallelly::availableCores(), without needing the parallelly package, and takes about as long as reading a few environment variables. It is the smallest of the values below that apply.

Resource limits. A cpus given explicitly is capped at the smallest of these alone:

  • The logical cores online (physical cores with options(parallelly.availableCores.logical = FALSE)).

  • The cores the process may run on: its CPU affinity, as set by taskset, numactl, cgroup cpusets (Docker's --cpuset-cpus), job schedulers that bind tasks to cores, or Windows' start /affinity and job objects.

  • A CPU quota, in whole cores: Linux cgroup v1 and v2 quotas (Docker's --cpus, Kubernetes CPU limits, systemd's CPUQuota) or a Windows job object's hard CPU rate cap.

  • The cores a job scheduler allocated on this node: Slurm (SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE, ...), PBS/Torque (PBS_NUM_PPN, NCPUS), LSF (LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC), SGE (the PE_HOSTFILE, NSLOTS), Fujitsu PJM (PJM_VNODE_CORE, PJM_PROC_BY_NODE) and HTCondor (_CONDOR_MACHINE_AD, _CONDOR_JOB_AD).

  • 2 under R CMD check --as-cran (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_), and 4 on Bioconductor's build machines.

  • options(ecodive.cpus = n), or the environment variable R_ECODIVE_CPUS.

Defaults. These lower n_cpus(), but not the cap on an explicit cpus:

  • The mc.cores option, or the MC_CORES environment variable.

  • BIOCPARALLEL_WORKER_NUMBER.

  • 1 in a worker process: one forked by, e.g., parallel::mclapply(), future's multicore plan or BiocParallel's MulticoreParam after ecodive was loaded, or a worker of a socket cluster (parallel, parallelly, future's multisession plan, snow), mirai or clustermq. Those workers already run side by side, so more threads in each would compete for the same cores. Give cpus to use more.

  • These options of parallelly (parallelly.availableCores.*, also read as future.availableCores.*, or the environment variables R_PARALLELLY_AVAILABLECORES_*), whether or not parallelly is installed: methods and methods.excludes (which of parallelly's methods above apply), fallback, custom, min, system, logical, threadsPerWorker, fraction, omit and max.

Settings that are missing, not numbers or less than 1 are ignored. Results are the same for any number of threads.

Examples

    n_cpus()
#> [1] 4
